**Part A**
To find the number of integers from 1 to 5,000 divisible by at least one of 6, 10, or 15, we use the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion:
- Divisible by 6: $\lfloor 5000/6 \rfloor = 833$
- Divisible by 10: $\lfloor 5000/10 \rfloor = 500$
- Divisible by 15: $\lfloor 5000/15 \rfloor = 333$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,10) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000/30 \rfloor = 166$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,15) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000/30 \rfloor = 166$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(10,15) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000/30 \rfloor = 166$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,10,15) = 30$: $\lfloor 5000/30 \rfloor = 166$

Total divisible by 6, 10, or 15:
$$833 + 500 + 333 - 166 - 166 - 166 + 166 = 1334$$

Now, subtract those among them also divisible by 19:
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,19) = 114$: $\lfloor 5000/114 \rfloor = 43$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(10,19) = 190$: $\lfloor 5000/190 \rfloor = 26$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(15,19) = 285$: $\lfloor 5000/285 \rfloor = 17$
- Divisible by $\text{lcm}(30,19) = 570$: $\lfloor 5000/570 \rfloor = 8$

By Inclusion-Exclusion for multiples of 19:
$$43 + 26 + 17 - 8 - 8 - 8 + 8 = 70$$

Remaining integers:
$$1334 - 70 = 1264$$
